title: Tesco Quits US and Takes $3.5 Billion Global Writedown
主要内容: Tesco, the UK-based supermarket giant, has decided to exit the US market, marking a significant strategic shift. The company announced a $3.5 billion global writedown as part of its restructuring efforts. This decision aims to eliminate redundancies and address onerous leasehold issues. The process of exiting the US market is expected to take at least three more months to complete. Despite these challenges, Tesco has maintained its dividend payment at 14.76 pence. The move reflects broader strategic adjustments in response to market conditions and operational inefficiencies. Tesco, Britain's largest retailer, announced it would exit the U.S. market and take a $3.5 billion global writedown, as it sought to rebuild after a year of falling profits for the first time in two decades. The company, the world's third-largest retailer after Wal-Mart Stores and Carrefour, said abandoning its loss-making Fresh & Easy in the U.S. would mean restructuring and other one-off costs of 1 billion pounds ($1.5 billion).
